title: Faith enters the boy
theme: Watching the gifts being led away, the young Naciketas is seized by śraddhā and begins to think.

words.context: Śaṅkara: a child not yet of age («अप्राप्तप्रजननशक्तिं बालमेव»)

words.gram: pres. passive participle, f. loc. pl.
words.role: locative absolute: ‘as the gifts were being led’

words.context: Śaṅkara: «श्रद्धा आस्तिक्यबुद्धिः» — conviction that the teaching is true, prompted by care for his father

sandhi.rule: aḥ before a becomes o and the a is elided (written with avagraha): P. 6.1.114 (हशि च) by extension and P. 6.1.109 (एङः पदान्तादति).

morphology.note: Present passive participle of nī, ‘lead’, locative plural agreeing with dakṣiṇāsu: a locative absolute, ‘while the gifts were being led [to the priests]’.
Plural. Raṅgarāmānuja discusses at length why dakṣiṇā, the sacrificial fee, is plural here: one fee per rite, but several priests receive their shares.
Imperfect middle of man, ‘think’. What he thought is given in the next mantra.

translation.literal: Faith entered him, being [yet] a boy, while the gifts were being led away; he thought:
translation.readable: Though he was only a boy, as the cows were led away to the priests, faith took hold of him, and he thought:

anvaya: दक्षिणासु नीयमानासु कुमारम् सन्तम् तम् ह श्रद्धा आविवेश । सः अमन्यत ॥
syntax: One sentence with a locative absolute (‘as the gifts were being led away’), a main clause (‘faith entered him, though a boy’) and a short second clause (‘he thought’), which leads into the next mantra, the content of his thought.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara and Raṅgarāmānuja both define śraddhā as āstikya-buddhi, conviction that the scripture’s teaching is true, and both say it was prompted by concern for his father’s good. The text itself only says that śraddhā ‘entered’ him.

ambiguities.topic: The end of the verse in Madhva’s text
ambiguities.note: Madhva’s text ends the verse at āviveśa and lacks ‘so ’manyata’, ‘he thought’ (corrections.json); it counts mantras 1–2 as one verse.

metre.name: prose
metre.note: Prose, 25 syllables as written; not metrical.

beginner: Naciketas is a boy, too young to have a part in the ritual. But as he watches the cows being led away as gifts to the priests, something happens to him: faith takes hold of him. In the Upaniṣads this word means more than belief. The commentators explain it as a settled conviction that what the scripture teaches is true, a conviction that makes one care how things are done. The boy sees the gifts, and he begins to think. The next verse tells us what he thought. The quiet point of this verse is that seriousness about truth can arise in anyone, even a child, and that it begins with simply looking at what is in front of you.
analogy: Like a child at a family celebration who notices, before any adult does, that something being done is not quite right.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: As the gifts were being led to the priests, śraddhā entered Naciketas, though he was only a boy, and he reflected.

commentary.q: What is the śraddhā that entered him?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Śaṅkara: «श्रद्धा आस्तिक्यबुद्धिः पितुर्हितकामप्रयुक्ता आविवेश प्रविष्टवती» — faith, the conviction that [the scripture] is true, prompted by the wish for his father’s good, entered him. Raṅgarāmānuja repeats the definition almost word for word: «आस्तिक्यबुद्धि पितुः हितकामप्रयुक्ता».

commentary.q: Why stress that he was a boy?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Śaṅkara glosses kumāram santam as a child not yet able to beget — «अप्राप्तप्रजननशक्तिं बालमेव» — that is, one who had no claim of his own in the rite. His concern is entirely for the father.

commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: Raṅgarāmānuja, as a ritualist, asks why dakṣiṇāsu is plural when a rite has one fee, and answers that the fee is reckoned per priest, so there are many: «ऋत्विग्बहुत्वापेक्षया दक्षिणाबहुत्वसम्भवात् दक्षिणासु इति बहुवचनम्».

advaita.text: The boy’s śraddhā is āstikya-buddhi prompted by care for his father («पितुर्हितकामप्रयुक्ता»): the qualification of the future student is shown before the teaching begins.

visistadvaita.text: The same definition — «श्रद्धा – आस्तिक्यबुद्धि पितुः हितकामप्रयुक्ता» — with a ritual discussion of the plural dakṣiṇāḥ.

schools.disagreement: None of substance here; Madhva’s bhāṣya has no separate comment on this mantra, which his text joins to the first.

parallels.quote: श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः
parallels.note: The Gītā’s claim that a person is made of śraddhā, and is what his śraddhā is, gives the word the weight it carries here: the boy’s faith decides what he will become.

contemporary.text: The person who notices that something is wrong is not always the one in charge; here it is the youngest present. Conscience does not wait for seniority. This is a modern reflection, not the text’s claim.

reflect.beginner: Have you ever noticed something wrong that the adults or seniors around you did not?
reflect.deeper: Is śraddhā, as the commentators define it, something one decides to have, or something that ‘enters’?
reflect.practice: Today, look carefully at one routine you take part in and ask whether it is done as it should be.

flags.note: Madhva’s text lacks ‘so ’manyata’ and counts mantras 1–2 as its verse 1 (corrections.json).
